AURA.role: four-role hypothesis framing and Telegram interface

persistent_memory_counterexample.interpretation: Persistent graph memory can store all visited residuals but does not create a polynomial semantic quotient.

representation_test.boundary: Only syntactic permutation is normalized; semantic equivalence still needs a certificate or potentially hard reasoning.

hidden_selector_cost.interpretation: A four-option interface can hide repeated exact SAT searches inside selection.

proof_dag_positive_result.interpretation: HRain is useful as a proof/provenance DAG when every node already carries typed, checkable semantics.

iNaiHR.security_note: A client-side API credential is present in public frontend source and should be revoked/removed.

AURA.best_role: typed hypothesis framing and Telegram interface
AURA.risk: role consensus and interpretation are not proof
AURA.security_note: Backend interpretation is inserted as HTML and must be sanitized.

HRain.best_role: persistent provenance graph, hierarchy and import/export
HRain.risk: memory stores visited states but does not create semantic quotient

surviving_conjecture: iNaiHR may generate candidates, AURA may type them, and HRain may preserve provenance, but P=NP still requires a single polynomially costed policy that emits a verified SAT witness or UNSAT Tear for every CNF.
verdict: The fusion materially improves research organization, memory, counterexample retention and soundness. It does not reduce worst-case SAT complexity.
